context: Owner (2026-11-08): "speed up everything else please, it needs to run flawless (don't mind about the combat if you can't do anything else about it)". FPS TARGET: a steady 30 fps on every screen and platform (GBA, PS1, Dreamcast), no hitches; combat stays as SP8 left it. SPEED DEFAULTS: pixel-changing steps (a held frame, a short fade over a load, a stand-in or the previous picture for 1-3 ticks, a "Saving..." card) are allowed where exact steps cannot reach 30; each one is listed in the docs with before / after screenshots. The measurements and the package list this wave works from: docs/design/held/SPEED_AUDIT2.md (sections 4-6); the tooling: tools/speed2.py, make -C gba test-speed2 / profile-speed2, ps1/harness/speed2.sh, dc/harness/speed2.sh (docs/GBA.md "Speed tour 2" and "Speed wave 2", docs/PS1.md "Speed tour 2"). Landed so far: S2-1..S2-8, S2-12, S2-13 and the analog sticks (ST1). A separate agent is re-measuring every scene right now (speed audit 3, branch fut-sa3): do not duplicate its work.

packages.title: PS1 resident memory headroom
packages.brief:
PS1 resident memory: get real headroom back.
State: the PS1 game EXE (boot FMV linked) ends 65,952 B below the stack top (commit e89f329); ps1/tools/elf2exe.py fails the build under 65,536 B, so 416 B are left. The plan gate is 72 KB. Two packages already hit this wall (docs/PS1.md "RAM fix 2026-11-08"). The waves that follow (Talk on the PS1: about +4 KB resident; 24 new levels; 1,500 creator parts) all add PS1 code, so this package must free far more than the 6 KB that reaches the gate.
Goal: at least 72 KB below the stack top is the minimum to land; aim for 96 KB or more (stretch: the old 128 KB goal), with NO scene slower than before: every PS1 scene that holds 30 fps today still holds it (PCSX-Redux: sh ps1/harness/speed2.sh for all groups before and after, plus the perf scripts docs/PS1.md names for the hot scenes; combat fps must not drop either).
Measure first: a resident ledger by object file and by symbol from the link map / nm --size-sort of ps1/build/doomogachi.elf (.text, .rodata, .data, .bss separately; overlay groups apart from the resident EXE). Write it into docs/PS1.md.
Where the bytes usually are:
 - code that is resident but used by one scene family only: move it into that family's overlay group (ps1/tools/ovl_plan.py PARTS; docs/PS1.md explains the overlay slot and its size). Usually the biggest wins.
 - resident read-only tables that could be read from the disc when needed, as TEXT.BIN, SFX.BIN and the language tables already are;
 - -O2 files in DOOMO_CORE_HOT (ps1/CMakeLists.txt) that do not need -O2 everywhere (hot loop kept -O2, the rest -Os), and ps1/src files not yet in DOOMO_PS1_COLD;
 - big .bss / .data statics (the CI step "Biggest PS1 statics" lists them): buffers that can shrink, be shared, or live in the scene scratch or an overlay's bss;
 - dead code and duplicated tables (the map shows what is kept; -ffunction-sections with --gc-sections if not already on).
Rules: no behaviour change and no pixel change (prove it with the PS1 harness checks the repo already has and game_smoke); the GBA and Dreamcast builds stay as they are unless a shared change is made on purpose for all three (then all gates). After each step: the margin and the fps of the scenes that step could slow; keep a table (step, bytes freed, fps before / after) in docs/PS1.md under a new section "RAM headroom 2026-11-12" and add the ledger row. A step that costs fps anywhere is dropped or reworked.
Also: make the PS1 build print a clear WARNING when the margin is under 72 KB (the plan gate), so CI logs show it long before the hard 64 KB failure (ps1/tools/elf2exe.py), and put the margin into the CI job summary (.github/workflows/ci.yml, the PS1 job) if that is cheap.

packages.title: Workshop without freezes
packages.brief:
Speed S2-9, the Workshop (docs/design/held/SPEED_AUDIT2.md section 6 row S2-9; sections 4 and 5 have the measurements): the weapon composition (weld_gfx outline + seg) blocks one tick for 260 ms three times a visit on the GBA (100 ms on the PS1); the workshop ran at 19-23 fps on the GBA and welding below 30.
Goal: a steady 30 fps and no frame over 33 ms in the workshop and welding windows of the speed2 scripts (gba/harness/scripts/speed2_*.txt: find the workshop / welding windows) on GBA and PS1, and no regression on the Dreamcast: the composition sliced across ticks with the old picture shown meanwhile (pixel-changing for the slice ticks: allowed, listed with before / after screenshots), composed ahead for the neighbours of the part under the cursor; the part list as a kept (retained) panel; and whatever else the profile of those windows shows.
A half-finished attempt from 2026-11-08 is saved as an uncommitted diff: docs/design/held/patches/wip/fut-s2-9.patch (core/include/doomo/weld.h, core/src/weld_gfx.c, core/src/workshop.c). Its first line is a marker ("=== UNCOMMITTED ==="): strip it, then try git apply -3. It was never reviewed or measured: read it critically, keep what is right, and delete that wip file in your final commit. S2-5 (landed since) already sped up the welding draws: re-measure before you decide what is left.

packages.title: Saves and loads without a frozen screen
packages.brief:
Speed S2-10, saves and loads without a frozen screen (docs/design/held/SPEED_AUDIT2.md section 6 row S2-10, cause C7): the free-play save blocks one frame for 11.4 s on the GBA, 11.6 s on the PS1 and 4.5 s on the Dreamcast; title -> New story has a 2.3 s and a 1.1 s frame on the PS1 and 2.07 s on the GBA; a new island 2.0 s (GBA) / 1.77 s (PS1).
Goal: no single frame over about 100 ms anywhere in those flows on GBA, PS1 and Dreamcast, with the screen alive at 30 fps the whole time: the save streams a few KB per tick behind an animated "Saving..." card (GBA flash: sector erase + program per tick; PS1 memory card: its 128 B sectors per tick; Dreamcast VMU: blocks per tick); town generation for New story / a new island spread over the ticks of a short fade (G-LD of the first speed audit: fades over loading freezes are approved).
Must hold: the saved bytes are identical to today's (make -C gba test-coresave and test-save, ps1/harness/memcard_check.py, dc/tests/vmu), old saves load, and a save stays atomic: a power cut or a reset in the middle leaves the previous save intact (test it by cutting at several points on each platform's host test). Pixel-changing (the card and the fades): allowed, with before / after screenshots.
A half-finished attempt from 2026-11-08 is saved as an uncommitted diff: docs/design/held/patches/wip/fut-s2-10.patch (core save.c / town.c, plat_ext.h, plat_weak_ext.c, gba loadfade.c / main.c, ps1 gfx.c / memcard.c, the PS1 harness). Its first line is a marker ("=== UNCOMMITTED ==="): strip it, then try git apply -3. It was never reviewed or measured: read it critically, keep what is right, and delete that wip file in your final commit.
Mind the PS1 memory: new PS1 code goes into -Os files or an overlay group; the lander checks the margin.
